title: re-authentication on relaunch/restart
body:
### What is the issue?

This issue appears in v1.90.2 when installing the macOS standalone .pkg; v1.88.4 (both standalone and App Store) does not exhibit the problem.

- After installing the macOS standalone .pkg v1.90.2, Tailscale requires re-authentication on reboot and when the Tailscale app is relaunched (same behavior described in the referenced issue).
- v1.88.4 (standalone and App Store) does not require re-authentication.

Reference: https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/8780

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install the macOS standalone .pkg for Tailscale v1.90.2.
2. Reboot the Mac or quit and relaunch the Tailscale app.
3. Observe that Tailscale requires re-authentication (login and approval).

### Are there any recent changes that introduced the issue?

_No response_

### OS

macOS

### OS version

Ventura 13.7.8

### Tailscale version

1.90.2

### Other software

_No response_

### Bug report

_No response_

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
Hi
To anyone reading this thread: I talked with support. They indicated that TS has identified the issue as "_likely due to a bug with Tailscale [trying to store] the node’s state in the TPM secure storage rather than directly on the filesystem, on older macOS versions._" and they are "_working on this, but don’t have an immediate timeline to share on the fix_".

Apple doesn't have TPM so I guess they are talking about the _enclave_, which indeed only exists on Apple Silicon macs.

Recommendation is to stick to v1.88.4 until further notice.

comments.author: participant26
comments.body:
I experienced this on 1.98.8 (macOS 12.7.6, 2015 Intel MBP): each time I disconnect and reconnect, I have to "add this device" to my tailnet. It gets a new name and IP (`<hostname>-<n>`).

There also seems to be a problem where sometimes opening preferences or other windows from the menu participant28 opens an application on the dock, and quitting that application icon kills the menu participant28 icon. But just starting Tailscale.app only opens the menu participant28 (no dock icon), so it doesn't seem like that's intentional.

After following the [previously posted instructions](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/17645#issuecomment-4180502136) to uninstall, purge remaining files, and install 1.88.4 (including checking the checksum 😄): I removed the old devices from the tailnet, connected the device, unchecked "automatically install updates" in preferences.

- I see the [same account screen bug as others](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/17645#issuecomment-4793192951)
- The admin console shows me connected, but the menu participant28 says "Tailscale is starting"
- `/…/Tailscale status` says I'm connected, too
- Connections to other devices work
- Reconnecting worked (no IP change, no new device) and solved the "Tailscale is starting" status (now the menu participant28 shows connected).

🤷 I would not say this is fixed for older macOS yet; [sounds like they are still having issues with handling the Intel silicon](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/17645#issuecomment-3530299699).

comments.author: participant27
comments.body:
Since the fix is committed but won’t land until the next major release, here’s a workaround for anyone stuck on 1.98.x in the meantime. It avoids downgrading to 1.88.4 and may also be useful for verifying the fix once it ships.

### **Workaround (no downgrade)**

Opt out of keychain-backed state storage via the `EncryptState` policy:

```bash
sudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/io.tailscale.ipn.macsys.plist EncryptState -bool false
```

Then quit and relaunch Tailscale.

State returns to /Library/Tailscale/tailscaled.state, and both login state and serve config now survive quit/relaunch and full reboots on this machine.

### **Environment**

- MacBook Pro (2017, Intel i7)
- macOS Ventura 13.7.5 (22H527)
- Tailscale 1.98.8 standalone

This also affects `tailscale serve`: the CLI reports Serve as started, but `tailscale serve status` immediately reports no configuration because the Serve configuration is stored in the same state backend.

### **What I observed**

Every attempt to persist state to the keychain fails.

The extension first attempts `SecItemUpdate` (which fails because the item does not exist), falls back to `SecItemAdd`, and then fails while attempting to write into `/Library/Keychains/`:

```text
io.tailscale.ipn.macsys.network-extension: [general] - SecureStorage.saveData: update tailscale-machinekey in keychain: no such item
io.tailscale.ipn.macsys.network-extension: (Security) SecItemAdd
io.tailscale.ipn.macsys.network-extension: (Security) [com.apple.securityd:atomicfile] create /Library/Keychains/System.keychain.sb-06b3bec7-Zsq1mj: Operation not permitted
io.tailscale.ipn.macsys.network-extension: [general] - SecureStorage.saveData: add tailscale-machinekey: failed to add item (72 bytes) to keychain: 100001: UNIX[Operation not permitted]
io.tailscale.ipn.macsys.network-extension: [general] - prefs_save failed: err("add tailscale-machinekey: failed to add item (72 bytes) to keychain: 100001: UNIX[Operation not permitted]")
```

The same sequence repeats for:

- `tailscale-machinekey`
- `tailscale-profiles`
- `tailscale-id-profile-*`
- `tailscale-current-profile`
- `tailscale-logdata`

As a result, no persistent state is ever saved. The node functions normally while running, but after every restart it registers as a new device (`hostname-1`, `hostname-2`, etc.), and `tailscale serve` configuration is likewise lost.

The kernel log shows the underlying denial:

```text
kernel: (Sandbox) Sandbox: io.tailscale.ipn.macsys.network(4287) deny(1) file-write-create /Library/Keychains/System.keychain.sb-520fea41-ieQ7HY
kernel: (Sandbox) Sandbox: io.tailscale.ipn.macsys.network(4287) deny(1) file-write-create /Library/Keychains/System.keychain.sb-520fea41-ZfR6jw
```

### **Possible explanation**

One log line from the GUI may be relevant:

```text
Tailscale: (Security) [com.apple.securityd:keychain] System Keychain Always Supported set via feature flag to disabled
```

My interpretation is that, on Ventura, keychain-backed state storage is attempting a code path that ultimately requires creating temporary files under `/Library/Keychains/`. Those writes are denied by the Network Extension sandbox, so every persistence attempt fails.

I can’t say with certainty whether that’s the root cause, but it matches the observed behavior and the kernel sandbox denials.

The failure is also effectively silent: `prefs_save failed` is logged, but the client otherwise continues operating normally, so nothing appears wrong until the next restart.

Happy to re-enable EncryptState and verify keychain writes succeed on this Ventura/Intel machine once the next major release is out, if that's useful.

`BUG-85ce54dbf0592c47550bd36bd1a66bc4e8f54e6a62cc332431969a2e8c0e1c77-20260706184225Z-3421bafeb9495182`
